label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Sizwe, first of all, congratulations on the wedding. Now take a breath — and leave that key **OUT**.

**Do not crank it again.** Every time you turn it over, the high-pressure pump is trying to run on petrol, which doesn’t lubricate it like diesel. That can score or wear the pump and damage the injectors. Kobus means well, but that’s old Land Rover/oom-in-winter advice. Your 2019 D-Max is common rail and can’t take that gamble.

**Don’t top it up with diesel either.** The petrol is still in there. Mixing does nothing except give me more contaminated fuel to drain.

You drove it and cranked it repeatedly, so I’ll be straight: damage is possible. But it’s **not automatically a finished engine or a R40 000 bill**. It needs a proper inspection before anyone promises either outcome. If the pump and injectors are OK, the usual job is drain the tank, flush the lines, fit a new fuel filter and bleed it — generally around **R2 500 to R4 500**. I can’t promise your total tonight without seeing it.

Tonight:

- Key out. No “just one last try”.
- Arrange a **tow, not a drive**. Check your insurance policy/app first; most have roadside assistance or towing, so don’t pay a tow oke cash before checking.
- **Borrow a bakkie for tomorrow anyway** for the cake and sound system. Don’t plan your wedding around a drained tank. The cake has been through enough.

My shop is in **Umbilo**, open **Saturday 7–12**. Get it towed to me and Thabo, my guy, can drain it first thing if the inspection says that’s all it needs.

And you’re not the first laaitie, trust me. In 1995, my first year as an apprentice, I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells that story at every braai. One customer did your trick twice in the same year at the same garage; we made him a sticker for his fuel flap.

So: hands off the key, sort the tow, sort the borrowed bakkie, and go be a groom. We’ll worry about the D-Max in the morning.
